First, note that the index $n$ starts from $4.$ However, it is still a geometric series because it is in the form
$\sum a{r}^{n}.$

In this case, the first term is ${a}_{4},$ and so the sum to infinity ${S}_{\infty }$ of this geometric series is given by

$$
{S}_{\infty }=\frac{{a}_{4}}{1-r},\,|r|<1.
$$

For the first few terms, we have:

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{4} & ={(\frac{2}{3})}^{4}=\frac{16}{81} \\ {a}_{5} & ={(\frac{2}{3})}^{5}=\frac{32}{243}\end{aligned}
$$

The common ratio is

$$
r=\frac{{a}_{5}}{{a}_{4}}=\frac{(\frac{32}{243})}{(\frac{16}{81})}=\frac{2}{3}.
$$

So, the sum of the series is

$$
\begin{aligned}{\sum }_{n=4}^{\infty }{(\frac{2}{3})}^{n} & =\frac{{a}_{4}}{1-r} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{16}{81})}{(1-\frac{2}{3})} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{16}{81})}{(\frac{1}{3})} \\  & =\frac{16}{27}.\end{aligned}
$$
